Central Stanton: Fifty-four of sixty first-place votes for a champion that just sent eight players to the draft, three of them in the first round — Katarina Bernhardt went second overall, DeAndre Rowwell sixth. The voters don't care because the title-game cast is back: Minato Watanuki threw for 272 yards and three scores in Chapel Rock as a freshman, Thomas Anyteng caught all three, and corner Xavier Farrow had two of the four interceptions that decided it. Zainab Cisse is the best cover man in the country. The eighth-hardest schedule opens with Kaji Daun at home in week 1.
Eona: The defending champion of 2038 lost the 2039 final and then went shopping: DeAndre Kingsbrook, the coordinator behind Rogaela State's offense, and Pranav Langdale from Ciarralotta Tech's defense are both in the building. Chiara Marshworth threw four interceptions in the title game as a sophomore and is the most interesting quarterback in Roiland because of it. Three draftees in the first three rounds, five transfers in. The second-hardest schedule: Skeenerland State in week 1, Central Stanton in week 6, both at home.
Kaji Daun: Nine wins and a playoff trip, then the offseason cost them Carlos Lopez, whose offense was good enough to earn him the Ediville State head job; Fatima Larsen replaced him by poaching Brunhilde Stanhope out of North Verigon. The quarterback was drafted in the second round, so the offense runs through Haneya Vesoviy, a senior who lines up everywhere. Six blue-chips in a sixteen-man class. Week 1 is at Central Stanton.
Tengus State: Eleven wins, 7-2, and the Power North title — then Widad El-Najjar took his offense to the Northlight head job and four players left through the portal against three arriving. The voters have them fourth anyway on the strength of the defense: Bhaskar Ramasekaran is the best interior lineman in the league, and five-star Amara Amateng arrives at linebacker to play next to him. Only one player drafted. The 74th-hardest schedule is kind.
Roosevelt: Twelve wins and 8-1 in the Western Coast with only two players lost to the draft. Friedrich Fuafolau, who came over from Crimson Mount a year ago, and Armand Lamont give them the best front seven west of the Great Fourteen, and Kenya Ademah, a five-star safety, headlines a nineteen-man class with six blue-chips. Sione Baker's third year. The schedule is the 71st-hardest, and nine of the twelve are in conference.
Rogaela State: Seven and five with one of the most talented rosters in the country, and then Eona came and took the offensive coordinator. Gudrun Rosenwetter, Dimitrios Gradovsky and Itsuki Nagamaki are three of the best skill players anywhere, which is why the projection — 9.6 wins — is the highest of any power-conference team. Both coordinators are new to their chairs. Two titles in the last five years. The question is whether the people calling the plays can keep up with the people running them.
Leafette: Nine players drafted, more than any programme in the country — the quarterback, two receivers and the running back among them. What's left is a 12-3, 7-2 Jyras Bay roster with its coaching staff intact, six blue-chips in a class of nineteen (the best by total stars in the league, tied with Roosevelt), and Sione Hightree arriving from Mount Cairn to play quarterback. The poll has them seventh; the projection says eight wins. Somewhere in between is a team that depends entirely on week-1 quarterback play.
Stanton: Nine wins and 6-3 with a staff in its fifth year together, nobody in through the portal and nobody out. Xinyi Songzheng is the best running back in the Great Fourteen; Yaping Fukamura the best safety. Rasheed Fenbury, the safety opposite him, went first overall in the draft. The 14th-hardest schedule has Central Stanton, Kaji Daun and Ranroman on it.
Skeenerland State: Twelve wins, 7-2, and a programme that has never won a national title. Isamu Yamasato and Chenguang Beisha are back; Abiodun El-Ghazali is a sophomore quarterback with a full season behind him. The offensive coordinator left for Central Stanton and the replacement is in his first year. Six blue-chips in an eleven-man class, and a 4-3 portal. Opens at Eona, which will say a lot about the ninth-place vote.
Eternal Fox: The first lower-division team in the preseason top ten in years, and two voters have them first. A 13-1 East Forest champion with the whole offense back — Obinna Stoneston at quarterback, Tomavaw Norrevei at tight end — and only one player drafted. The projection is 10.1 wins because the schedule is the 144th-hardest of 152: the non-conference is Perri Park, Tasson State and a subdivision guest. Last title 1984.
Hatesei: Twelve wins and a semifinal, then the offseason took both coordinators — Efrain Baldavanti left to run Sacred Tomb, and Poppy Hollerbach promoted from within on both sides. Haruto Kamikubo is the senior corner the defense is built around; Moonsik Sakanuma, the safety next to him, went in the first round. Five-star receiver Wesley Holmtveit is the gem of a six-blue-chip class. October is Eona, Central Stanton and Kaji Daun in four weeks.
Yrei Trobniy: Eleven wins and 7-2 in the Western Coast, with the running back and the quarterback both drafted. The replacement under center is Sungmin Zhenbin, a five-star true freshman — either the story of the year or an 8-4 season. Isamu Hu-Ho and Jaehyun Nam-Mok are the juniors who make the rest of it go. Nobody left through the portal; six blue-chips signed.
Ranroman: The hardest schedule in Roiland: Kaji Daun, Hatesei, Eona, Stanton and the rivalry game at Ranroman State, five of the nine conference games on the road. Kazimir Katamura lost nothing important to the draft and signed only five players, all of them blue-chips, the smallest class in the top 25 by a distance. Prokopis Eastworth is the sophomore receiver who will be the next star here. The offensive coordinator is in his second year.
Kaji Kita: Eleven wins and 8-1 in the Power North, then Shreya Peiqiao retired at seventy. Ebony Anywale comes over from Ciarralotta State's defense for her first head job and inherits a staff that stayed. Dieter Schwarzstein anchors the line as a senior, and five-star Veronique Quisveiro joins him as a freshman. The quarterback was drafted in the second round. The season ends with Tengus State and Kaji Daun back to back.
North Hatesei: Four and eight, 2-7 in the Great Fourteen — and the most storied programme in the sport, which is why the voters have them 15th anyway. Twenty-one national titles, the last in 2030; the defensive coordinator left to run West Hatesei State and both coordinators are new. Tuilagi Spottedrobe is the best tight end in the conference. One blue-chip in a thirteen-man class is the thinnest haul in the top 25, and the sixth-hardest schedule won't help.
Ciarralotta State: Eleven wins and 7-2 in the Broad South, then the defensive coordinator took the Kaji Kita job; Imani Latu answered by raiding Aliyah Radovsky from Diamond City to replace her. Taiga Myeong-Seong, the Ryskamp winner, was drafted; Oliver Langshaw comes in from Underwood to replace him, with Najwa El-Bakri back at running back. Five-star safety Bozena Krasyshyn headlines a six-blue-chip class in a ten-man group.
Verigon: Eleven wins and 7-2 in the Mountain Valley. Koharu Yezhen, the best player on the defense, went third overall; Rocio Santarini is the junior safety who has to carry it without him. Malsook Yacoub, the quarterback who starred at Chapel Rock, is the best portal pickup in the conference, and Abena Upshaw comes in from Krobe State to run the offense he'll play in. Five in, nobody out.
Crayellan State: The best quarterback in Roiland. Chengfei Pyeong-Seok is a junior with two full seasons behind him, and Thomas Thorncroft went and got him Iosefa Faitai — the receiver who was the most productive player on Crimson Mount's 12-5 team — and Kyungja Tsukabe from Will Tech to call the plays. Twelve wins and 8-1 last year. The defense lost two of its best to the draft; whether it holds is the whole question.
Ranroman State: Six and six with a top-five roster, and the carousel finally moved: Litowa Mesteniy comes in from Orlot Western for his first power-conference job and kept both coordinators. Keyto Kovaw is the best young linebacker in the conference; George Wintercott and Peizhi Xiangtan are a receiving pair any quarterback would want. A three-man signing class, all blue-chips, and the seventh-hardest schedule. Titles in 2034 and 2037.
UNN: Eight players drafted — the quarterback and a defensive lineman in the first round, a receiver and a tackle in the second — from a 7-5 team. Esperanza Caraobruno is in her second year. Sachiko Masumaki, a junior tackle, is the best player left, and an eighteen-man class brought five blue-chips. The ninth-hardest schedule, with Eona and Central Stanton in the last two weeks.
Ciarralotta Tech: Seven and five, then Eona took Pranav Langdale and the offense he built; both coordinators are new. Jack Rocherive is the best kicker in the country and Sunita Lozano a senior linebacker who should have gone in the draft and didn't. The projection says 8.9 wins on a middling schedule; the poll's 21st-place vote says the voters trust the roster more than the staff.
Marines: Ten wins and a Brass Belt title with a roster built on the line — Anselmo Maroncelli and Viggo Vinter are both tackles, and the two draftees were linemen too. One blue-chip in a thirteen-man class. The lower division's second-ranked team draws the 83rd-hardest schedule, with North Hatesei at home in week 9 and Eona Navy to finish.
Orlot: Six and six, 3-6 in the Great Fourteen, with a roster everyone agrees is better than that — Bertram Lorrovei is the best offensive lineman in the country, Mariana Valmayor a senior safety with a draft grade — and the voters have run out of patience at 23rd. Kalani Almeida lost his defensive coordinator to the Cherry Lake head job and poached Tessa Onyeemeka from Barhold to replace him. Three blue-chips in seventeen is a thin class for this roster. Central Stanton on the road in week 4.
Dietsche: Seven and five under Sora Yamamoto, with both coordinators in their second year and the quarterback drafted in the fifth round. Bertram Havtveit, a sophomore tight end, is the player to watch; five blue-chips signed in a class of sixteen. The 18th-hardest schedule finishes with four of the last five against the Jyras Bay's top half.
North Verigon: Nobody drafted, four transfers in, one out — the most intact roster in the top 25 — and 7-5 last year. Lucia Duregard leads the line; the defensive coordinator who built it, Brunhilde Stanhope, left for Kaji Daun, and Barnaby Brookberry replaced her by luring Ravi Kamau out of the Underwood head job. The projection is 8.2 wins. Opens at Rogaela State.
